nodes.label: rendercv-web-backend
nodes.rationale: FastAPI backend that wraps the rendercv core, imported as an editable path dependency, as a small HTTP service.

nodes.label: Editable path dependency on core
nodes.rationale: The backend imports rendercv as an editable path dependency and calls the same pipeline the CLI calls, so render and validate behaviour cannot diverge from core and core edits take effect without reinstalling.

nodes.label: uv-only Python tooling policy
nodes.rationale: Everything Python goes through uv (Python 3.12+); pip and direct python invocations are forbidden to keep the environment reproducible.

nodes.label: Four document tabs (CV, Design, Locale, Settings)
nodes.norm_label: four document tabs (cv, design, locale, settings)

nodes.label: Two-way form / raw-YAML sync
nodes.rationale: Each tab offers a schema-generated form and a raw YAML mode kept in sync both ways, so power users and form users edit the same document.

nodes.label: RenderCV Web Editor
nodes.rationale: Browser CV editor built on top of this repository's Python core rather than a rewrite, so rendering and validation cannot drift from the core pipeline.

nodes.label: Root CLAUDE.md code conventions
nodes.rationale: Code conventions in the root CLAUDE.md apply to Python in web/backend as well as to the core.

nodes.label: Single shared setup/run/test doc in ../README.md
nodes.rationale: Install, run, and test instructions are written once for both halves of the application in web/README.md so the two workspace READMEs cannot drift.

nodes.label: Anonymous CV merge on first sign-in
nodes.rationale: CVs written while anonymous are merged into the account on first sign-in, and the same happens on a second browser, so nothing is lost by signing in later.
nodes.norm_label: anonymous cv merge on first sign-in

nodes.label: Anonymous signed-cookie session
nodes.rationale: The app has no login requirement: a signed cookie gives each browser an anonymous session and CVs belong to that session.

nodes.label: /api/auth/google/callback redirect URI
nodes.rationale: The Authorized redirect URI must match character for character, including the https scheme and trailing slash, otherwise Google returns redirect_uri_mismatch.

nodes.label: Optional Google sign-in
nodes.rationale: Sign-in is purely additive - it only enables sharing CVs across browsers and devices; the anonymous cookie session remains the default full-function mode.

nodes.label: RENDERCV_WEB_ALLOWED_ORIGINS
nodes.rationale: Comma-separated list of frontend origins allowed to call the API; only needed when the frontend is served from a different origin than the API.

nodes.label: RENDERCV_WEB_HTTPS
nodes.rationale: Set to 1 when serving over HTTPS so the session cookie carries the Secure flag; unset means the cookie travels in readable form.

nodes.label: RENDERCV_WEB_SECRET
nodes.rationale: Signs the session cookie and must be set before deploying; the fallback is a hardcoded string in a public repository, so anyone could forge a validly signed session cookie and read other people's CVs. The backend only logs a warning instead of refusing to start.

nodes.label: Cross-origin CORS configuration
nodes.rationale: Same-origin deployments behind a reverse proxy need nothing; split origins must declare the frontend origin because the session cookie is sent with credentials and the browser rejects every request on an inexact origin match. The symptom is misleading - the page loads but sign-in and saving silently fail, with only a CORS console error as evidence.

nodes.label: provider_available: false hides sign-in UI
nodes.rationale: When OAuth is unconfigured the backend reports provider_available: false and the UI hides every sign-in control, so there are never dead buttons.

nodes.label: npm run test:e2e
nodes.rationale: Requires a backend running against a single-use database, per the shared README in web/.

nodes.label: Playwright end-to-end suite
nodes.rationale: Drives a real browser against a real backend, which makes it the only gate where a mistake destroys data.

nodes.label: uv sync --extra postgres
nodes.rationale: Installing the Postgres driver is the most frequently skipped deploy step; without it the backend dies at startup.

nodes.label: RENDERCV_WEB_DATABASE_URL
nodes.rationale: Accepts any SQLAlchemy-style URL so Postgres works without code changes; leaving it unset falls back to a file SQLite database that is lost on every container restart.

nodes.label: Default SQLite database file
nodes.rationale: With no configuration the backend creates web/backend/data/rendercv_web.db relative to the current working directory.

nodes.label: Playwright frontend on port 5199
nodes.rationale: Playwright builds its own frontend on port 5199 rather than 5173 so it never contends with an open dev server.

nodes.label: Postgres URL normalization
nodes.rationale: Provider connection strings paste in as-is: postgres://, postgresql://, and postgresql+psycopg:// all work because the backend normalizes them to the installed driver.

nodes.label: Throwaway e2e database
nodes.rationale: Always point the e2e backend at a single-use database: running against the default web/backend/data/rendercv_web.db writes test CVs into your development data and makes bootstrap-order-dependent tests flaky.

nodes.label: Automatic upgrade_to_head migration at startup
nodes.rationale: The app lifespan runs upgrade_to_head so the database schema migrates automatically on boot; there is deliberately no manual alembic upgrade step, in dev or in deployment.

nodes.label: Core wrapper HTTP surface (validate, render, schema, theme defaults)
nodes.norm_label: core wrapper http surface (validate, render, schema, theme defaults)

nodes.label: /api/render backend renderer
nodes.rationale: The backend-rendered preview is the canonical renderer; the WASM path is the only route that skips it.

nodes.label: Vite /api proxy to port 8000
nodes.rationale: The Vite dev server proxies /api to the backend on port 8000, so both processes must be running for the app to work in development.

nodes.label: Playwright workers: 1
nodes.rationale: Deliberate single worker: the dev backend is one uvicorn process, and CPU-heavy Typst renders would block its event loop if run in parallel.

nodes.label: Per-layer green gates before PR
nodes.rationale: Core, backend, and frontend each own a separate test gate and all of them must be green before a PR is opened.

nodes.label: npm run build:wasm-assets
nodes.rationale: One-time ~30 MB asset build dropped into the gitignored static/wasm/ directory.

nodes.label: Pyodide
nodes.rationale: Runs the rendercv wheel in the browser to produce Typst source; Pyodide itself is loaded from the jsdelivr CDN.

nodes.label: Client-side WASM preview
nodes.rationale: An entirely in-browser render path that never calls /api/render; off by default and costing nothing until enabled, while the backend renderer stays the canonical one.

nodes.label: WASM preview known limitations
nodes.rationale: Only the classic theme's fonts ship; Pyodide comes from the jsdelivr CDN and a few pure-Python dependencies are fetched from PyPI at runtime; cold start is roughly 17-20 seconds and warm renders are under a second.
